reason: The report gives only a naive bivariate OLS on a sample trimmed by outcome (top/bottom 1%, N=1960). It has no pre-period controls, including productivity_2020. Adding the 2020 covariates cuts the estimate from about 2.5 to about 0.58, so confounding drives the headline 2.17. The post-treatment mgmt_rating_2023 control, which should not be used, flips the sign, so it was rightly left out, but the answer still isn't a credible causal effect.
